title: Greenfield's Transport Transformation: A Simulated Case Study
instructions: 阅读下面关于Greenfield城市交通变化的短文，然后回答问题。所有数据均为模拟教学材料，不是真实统计。请根据文章内容作答。
passage:
A. In 2005, the city of Greenfield had a simple transport system. Most people travelled by bus or by car. The bus network was small: only 12 bus lines served the whole city. About 60% of workers drove to work, and 30% took the bus. Only 10% walked or cycled. The roads were often busy, but traffic was not too bad. The city had one train station, but few people used it. The average commute time was 35 minutes, and air pollution levels were moderate. The city centre had limited parking, so many drivers parked on the streets, causing some congestion during rush hours. The city also had a small fleet of taxis, but they were expensive and most people used them only for special trips. The local government did not spend much on public transport in those days; the budget for buses and trains was very limited. Many bus stops had no shelters, and buses were often old and noisy. Cycling was not very safe because there were few cycle lanes. Children usually walked to school, but many parents drove them because they worried about traffic. The city had no park-and-ride facilities, so drivers had to find parking in the centre, which was difficult and costly. Overall, the transport system worked, but it was not efficient or comfortable.

B. By 2025, Greenfield had changed a lot. The city now has 36 bus lines—three times as many as in 2005. The number of train stations has increased from 1 to 4. The train is now the most popular way to travel: 40% of workers take the train to work. The bus is still important, but its share has fallen to 20%. Car use has dropped to 25%, and walking or cycling has risen to 15%. The city has also built 50 kilometres of new cycle lanes. The average commute time is now 28 minutes, and air pollution has decreased by 30%. The city centre has two new park-and-ride facilities, where drivers can leave their cars and take public transport. The bus fleet has been modernised: most buses are now electric and much quieter. There are also real-time information screens at major bus stops, so passengers know when the next bus will arrive. The city has introduced a bike-sharing scheme with 500 bicycles at 50 stations. Cycling is now much safer because the new cycle lanes are separated from car traffic. The government has also improved pedestrian areas in the city centre, making it easier and more pleasant to walk. These changes have made travelling around Greenfield more comfortable and reliable.

C. Why did these changes happen? First, the city government invested heavily in public transport. It spent twice as much on buses and trains in 2020 as it did in 2010. Second, fuel prices rose, so driving became more expensive. Third, the city introduced a congestion charge in the centre: drivers must pay £5 per day to enter the city centre. This money helps to pay for public transport. Finally, many people now care more about the environment. They want cleaner air and less noise. The government also launched a campaign to encourage cycling, which included free bicycle repair workshops and safe cycling lessons for adults. The campaign was supported by local businesses, which offered discounts to cyclists. Schools also took part by organising 'walk to school' weeks. These activities helped to change people's habits gradually. The government worked with transport experts to plan new bus routes that connect residential areas with workplaces and schools. Public meetings were held to listen to residents' opinions, and some routes were adjusted based on their feedback. This cooperative approach made the changes more acceptable to the public.

D. Not everything is perfect. Some people still need their cars, especially those who live far from bus stops. The congestion charge is unpopular with some drivers. Also, the trains are often crowded at peak times. However, most people agree that the transport system is better than it was 20 years ago. The city plans to add 10 more bus lines by 2030 and to double the number of cycle lanes. Greenfield is becoming a greener, more connected city. The government aims to reduce car use to 15% by 2035 and to increase the share of public transport to 60%. To achieve these goals, the city will continue to invest in infrastructure and to promote sustainable travel options. It also plans to introduce more electric buses and to expand the park-and-ride network. The city hopes that these measures will encourage more people to leave their cars at home and choose public transport, cycling, or walking. In the future, Greenfield aims to be a model for other cities that want to improve their transport systems.

grammar.title: 倍数与比例表达；比较结构；过去和现在数据的时态选择
grammar.explanation: 英语中表示倍数常用“times as many/much as”或“twice as much as”。比较两个时期的数据时，过去用一般过去时（如 in 2005, had, was），现在用一般现在时或现在完成时（如 now has, has fallen）。
grammar.example: The city now has 36 bus lines—three times as many as in 2005.

questions.prompt: In 2010, the town had 5 parks. Now it has 15 parks. The number of parks is now ______ it was in 2010.
questions.explanation: 15是5的三倍，所以用three times as many as。

questions.prompt: In 2000, the factory produced 100 cars a day. In 2020, it produced 200 cars a day. It produced ______ cars in 2020 as in 2000.
Choose the correct sentence about the past.
options: In 2005, most people travelled by bus.
In 2005, most people travel by bus.
In 2005, most people have travelled by bus.
In 2005, most people are travelling by bus.
answers: In 2005, most people travelled by bus.
questions.explanation: 2005年是过去时间，用一般过去时travelled。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about the present.
options: Now the city has 36 bus lines.
Now the city had 36 bus lines.
Now the city have 36 bus lines.
Now the city is having 36 bus lines.
answers: Now the city has 36 bus lines.
questions.explanation: now表示现在，用一般现在时has。
